gloss: calyx; stem end (of a tomato, persimmon, or eggplant)

definitions.gloss: calyx; the green cap and stem end of a fruit
definitions.explanation: The small leafy cap where the stem joins a fruit such as a tomato, persimmon, eggplant, or strawberry. In cooking it is the part you cut or pull off before eating.

examples.japanese: ⟦トマト→トマト：05192_tomato⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧へた⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧。
examples.english: Remove the stem end of the tomato.

examples.japanese: ⟦{柿|かき}→柿：04384_kaki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧へた⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{乾|かわ}いている→乾く：00786_kawaku⟧。
examples.english: The calyx of the persimmon is dry.

examples.japanese: {苺|いちご}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧へた⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{付|つ}けた→付ける：00761_tsukeru⟧まま⟦{洗|あら}う→洗う：00827_arau⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧っぽく⟦ならない→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: If you wash strawberries with the calyx still attached, they do not get watery.

notes:
Written {蒂|へた} or {萼|へた} in kanji, but almost always kana. A kitchen word rather than a botanical one; the technical term is ⟦{萼|がく}→萼：30519_gaku⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- へた⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to remove the calyx
- へた⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}り{落|お}とす→切り落とす：28973_kiriotosu⟧: to cut off the stem end
- へた⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{付|つ}いた→付く：01960_tsuku⟧まま: with the calyx still on
- へた⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{青|あお}い→青い：00586_aoi⟧: the calyx is green (a freshness sign)

USAGE:
A green, firm へた is the standard way of judging whether a tomato or persimmon is fresh, so the word turns up often in shopping and cooking advice.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{芯|しん}→芯：03888_shin⟧: core — the inner part of an apple or cabbage, not the outer cap
- ⟦{下手|へた}→下手：00703_heta⟧: unskillful — an unrelated homophone written with kanji
